documents.reason: Both versions explain that a reused box design can hide differences in piece count, so the label uses the manufacturer's title and count. The characters-and-sky example still explains why contributors describe the picture and difficult sections. Both group playable incomplete puzzles and mark the known gap with a removable note so each taker can choose. Both describe turning large sections over first and invite the last builder to check the backs and separate pieces before donation. The rewrite retains actual piece sizes and sample outlines for people with limited grip, the bottom shelf and visible age guidance for boxed children's puzzles, and the donor's clean image when a damaged lid needs a substitute. It retains the risk to neighboring boxes, inspection in good light and return to the donor for moisture or mildew. The short identifier still lets residents report problems after forgetting the title and lets volunteers match found pieces kept in labeled envelopes behind the desk. Both use incoming and outgoing counts at each opening to distinguish turnover from accumulation and schedule the next donation window. Both invite builders' photos and put the box identifier underneath so a neighbor can find the pictured puzzle.
